svg.aria-label: How the search works, as a five-stage pipeline. 1, belief sampling: the belief model reads the public history and gives each hidden card's holder probabilities, masked to the holders the public facts allow; 64 worlds are kept, drawn worlds are rejected by the history tests whl, whd, wht, rc and rcec, which apply to the first 512 draws, the plain sampler fills any shortfall after 2,560, and belief preparation over 0.25 s falls back to the Monte Carlo sampler. 2, candidates: up to 4,000 legal plays; the prior's summed card log-odds averaged over 64 root worlds rank them; 8 are admitted, the heuristic's play first, at most 2 per shape (div), la on a weak single lead, and sc8 probing singles on 8 worlds when a hand has more than 7 cards. 3, value pass: each trick is finished by greedy replies (lgf, lgfx, lgfd2000) and 512 positions are scored in batches of 128 as expected signed levels; ties within 0.02 go to trick points (tb); dtr and dtrx drop refused lead throws. 4, exact endgame at 7 cards or fewer a hand: partnership minimax with alpha-beta and a transposition table per world, averaged (ele, ed7, xf7, elm, elt, els1600), switching only on a strictly higher mean. 5, choose: the best mean wins; past the budget or on error the heuristic's choice is played. A 3 second budget timeline: the heuristic decides first, belief preparation up to 0.25 s, the exact lead stage starts only in the first half and its solve stops by 1.6 s, lgf stops at 2 s, both exact stages stop by 2.4 s, the budget ends at 3 s. Side lanes: declaration scores each option and passing on 64 deals (vd, vdef); the bury scores up to 64 candidate kitties on 32 belief-drawn worlds within 2 s (bwv, bbw).
